description: The line plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC) in percentage as a function of the co-occurrence number for five different methods: Base, MEND, FT, MEMIT, and ROME. The x-axis, labeled "Co-occurrence Number," is plotted on a logarithmic scale ranging from 1 to 1000, with tick marks at 10^1, 10^2, and 10^3. The y-axis, labeled "ACC (%)", is a linear scale ranging from 60 to 80. The "Base" method, represented by a black line with circular markers, shows a steady increase in accuracy from approximately 61.5% to 66.5%. The "MEND" method, shown with a brown line and diamond markers, starts at about 66% and rises to around 74%. The "FT" method, depicted with a blue line and triangle markers, begins at roughly 62.5% and increases to about 68%. The "MEMIT" method, represented by a purple line with pentagon markers, starts at approximately 66% and climbs to about 72.5%. The "ROME" method, shown with a green line and square markers, starts at around 72% and increases to approximately 77.5%. All methods exhibit a positive trend in accuracy as the co-occurrence number increases.
